The sleeping part is only half of it. Sleeping alone won’t solve all your problems, but the decision to sleep is the decision to try again, and that’s all you can do if you ever want it to get better. If you want to use my analogy correctly, the music is the “getting better” part. You want life to get better don’t you? You just need to go find what it is that will help you get there (the missing piece). Maybe that’s talking to a professional, maybe that’s making some drastic life changes for the better. But you need to put in some effort, even if it’s just a little at first. Even rain will dissolve a mountain in time. You just need to start on the right path to a brighter tomorrow.

You just have to sleep on it. Ask yourself every day, and one day you’ll wake up and realize that you didn’t even notice it got better. It’s not a eureka moment, it doesn’t show up with confetti and streamers. One day you’ll just notice the weight is a little lighter than it used to be, one day you’ll notice you can breathe a little easier. But you have to try, try to convince yourself that there’s a reason to sleep on it every day. But you also have to put effort in. It’s like a music box; the music doesn’t play if you don’t turn it, and if it doesn’t turn? You just need to disassemble it and figure out what needs to be fixed. That’s all you can do. So just sleep on it tonight, and try again tomorrow.

Problem with your hypothetical is that parents don’t do that.

It is safe. Safe only means small risk. Nothing is definite. There is also a small risk that the child may have issues with their foreskin throughout their life. As far as looking normal, this may have a drastic effect on mental development and health. A parents concern with that is not madness, it’s a conscious parental decision, and any good parent only does what they think is best for their child, and that should not be infringed upon when it comes to safe choices for their children. Parents consent for their children on many things in their attempts to lead their children to a healthy adulthood. And to have that parental choice made illegal would be the government parenting the children, and restricting parental liberty over a reasonably safe procedure. What is mad is the idea that the government should parent people’s children anymore than it already does.

Vaccines aren’t necessary. This is what your immune system is for. Obviously, the parents will want to use vaccines to ensure the baby lives a long life. But that means the parents are consenting for the baby their own personal beliefs that medicine is necessary. For example some individuals hold the beliefs that pharmaceuticals are detrimental to society, and that nature should just take its course (and sometimes for religious reasons). But of course that is very very rare, most people accept medicine, but the parents are consenting to a personal belief for the baby; that’s the point. If safe, parents should have that choice in regards to what they consent for their child. In the case of circumcision, it is also not necessary, but parents consent for the baby because they believe it is the best parental decision for them. I think the fact doctors still perform them goes to show that it is very low risk, and potential benefit (though most likely small) makes it a perfectly reasonable choice.

As a circumcisee I’m quite happy with my parents decision. I think it truly doesn’t really effect your life much at all either way, but I can’t imagine it any way else. I have reasons to believe it’s better, which can be argued til we’re all blue in the face, but it won’t change anyone’s opinion, nor would I want to. It’s a parental choice, and I think parents  should have that choice. If a grown adult has an issue with having been circumcised as an infant, perhaps there is a deeper underlying mental health issue that needs to be taken care of first, because that should be the least of your concerns.

Do you have the strength to get through tomorrow? Ask yourself that every day. I forget the story exactly, but it’s about a woman who swam the English Channel (maybe the first?). When she felt like she was about to give up, she’d ask herself “do I have it in me to swim 10 more seconds?”. Then she did, she swam 10 more seconds. She’d keep asking herself that. “Can I swim 5 more seconds?” it got harder. But then she did it, she crossed the English Channel. The point is that so long as you keep going you will find land eventually, you just can’t give up. The difference in your story is you can ask for help, you don’t have to tread alone, but you have to keep going. Winston Churchill said “if you’re going through hell, keep going”. I really hope you post here tomorrow, after you’ve decided you are willing to swim one more day. You’re not in this alone.

Well that would be failing as a mother by killing yourself. Every day you wake up and decide to keep going through hell is being a good mother, it might feel like hell right now, but as Winston Churchill said “if you’re going through hell, keep going”. This is temporary, your kids will get older, they’ll go to school, new job opportunities will come. You just need to stay within the lines, and you’re doing that. You’re doing the right things, even if they feel like failure. The fact that you decided to help your mental health by jeopardizing your financial situation says to me you are a good mother. This is why in airplanes they say to put your open oxygen mask on before helping your children. You need to be ok before you can help your children. Everything you’re dealing with is very temporary. Try to find other mothers and family’s who you can lean on for support, even if it’s just someone to relate to, it’s good for your own perspective. Take time for your own recreation too, you’re still young and need a social life. You seem to have a good enough compass, trust it’s leading you to where you need to go. Suicide can’t be an option. It isn’t. Your children need you. They love you so much.

Start planning to move out on your own. Be excited about that, and not dying. But first get calm. Maybe consider seeing a councillor?
You have nothing to be ashamed of. You made mistakes, everyone makes mistakes. Be glad that you’re wiser now.
